message.content: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon passes directly between the Earth and the Sun, casting its shadow onto the Earth’s surface. Because the Moon’s shadow is relatively small, only a narrow path experiences the total eclipse, while most locations see only a partial or no eclipse. The geometry of the Sun, Moon, and Earth must align just right, so the eclipse is visible only from specific regions on Earth.
